links.title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization

evidence: Abstract/Sec 1: Turbo Harness recycles artifacts from a completed outer-loop harness search into a playbook and trains an RL-fine-tuned editor (Qwen3.5-9B) to generate instance-specific patches to the global harness.

Table 1 (Sec 5.2): Turbo Harness beats Meta-Harness on all four agentic benchmarks (ALFWorld 70.7 vs 60.7, ScienceWorld 42.4 vs 35.1, DBBench 69.2 vs 65.0, WebShop 42.0 vs 40.0) and outperforms ReAct/Self-Refine/Reflection.
Table 2 (Sec 5.2): SWE-smith-MR pass rate rises 50.7→64.0 (Haiku) and 70.7→88.0 (Gemini) over Meta-Harness, with fewer steps (8.7 vs 23.1 Gemini) and lower cost ($0.046 vs $0.310).

Sec 5.5/Fig 3: ablation shows neither playbook alone (50.0%) nor RL alone (49.3%) beats Meta-Harness (50.7%); combined RL+playbook reaches 64.0%; RL-trained 9B editor (64.0%) matches frozen Opus-4.6 editor (61.3%) and beats Sonnet-4.5 (55.3%).
Appendix B.4: checkpoint selection on SWE-bench Verified by validation pass rate with exclusion of entropy-collapsed checkpoints (Haiku step 60 at entropy 0.066 excluded; step 10 selected).

Appendix B.5: costs cover only the execution model and exclude offline optimization and the one-time editor call; coding SEMs over three runs, TB2.1 over five runs; agentic benchmarks use one run each.
Appendix C.3: Harness-R1 comparison uses different runtimes and rollout budgets, and WebShop's 42.2 is author-reported; the comparison 'does not isolate the effect of the harness editor alone'.
Appendix A.2/A.3: SWE-smith-MR holds out issues within the same 25 repositories (not unseen repositories); TB2.1 uses only 45 training / 44 test tasks.
Appendix B.2/Table 4: full GRPO training configuration given (full-parameter FSDP, lr 1e-6, β=1e-3, per-benchmark group sizes/epochs/GPUs; WebShop uses a divergent tuned recipe).
Sec 6: limitations stated - effectiveness depends on quality/diversity of the completed global search, and editor training requires additional costly environment rollouts.

Appendix D.2: qualitative verbatim patches show executable-code edits (e.g., verification gate threshold 8→6, phase-budget relaxation) rather than prompt-only changes; TB2.1 examples are search-stage training-task edits because test patches were not persisted.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core agentic-LLM contribution: instance-adaptive agent harness optimization via an RL (GRPO)-trained small editor that patches a globally optimized harness using a playbook distilled from a prior search archive. Strong fit to Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, RL/RLHF training, and code-agent benchmarks. Novelty is moderate: the instance-adaptation premise is intuitive and builds on Meta-Harness, ACE playbooks, and concurrent JIT-Agent/Harness-R1; the 'recycle search exhaust into a per-instance patcher' framing is the fresh part. Rigor is solid but not airtight: seven benchmarks, SEM over 3 (coding) / 5 (TB2.1) runs, ablations isolating RL and playbook (64.0% vs 49.3%/50.0%/51.3%), reward-integrity safeguards, and honest confound disclosures; weaknesses include single-run agentic evaluations, tiny sets (50 issues SWE-smith-MR, 44 TB2.1 tasks), a WebShop-specific tuned GRPO recipe, and validation-based checkpoint selection. Evidence is quantitative with error bars and verbatim patch case studies, though one baseline is author-reported and the Harness-R1 comparison uses different runtimes/rollout budgets. Generalizability is decent across task families and two executors but untested for unseen repositories and cross-task editor transfer (acknowledged future work). Reproducibility is good: public code, full training tables, seeds, splits, and reward definitions.

primary_link.title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization

papers.summary: Automating the search for effective harnesses is an important step toward enabling agents to recursively self-improve. Existing harness optimizations typically produce a single global harness that is applied uniformly across task instances. However, a harness that works well on average may not be optimal for every instance. We introduce Turbo Harness, a framework that can adapt a globally optimized harness to each instance by reusing information generated during the original optimization process
papers.summary_zh: 現行代理執行外殼（harness）最佳化多半只產生一套全域外殼，套用到所有任務實例；然而在部分實例上最有效的外殼，未必對其他實例同樣理想，例如來自不同 GitHub 儲存庫的 SWE-Bench 題目往往需要不同的工作流程與驗證慣例。此外，外殼搜尋成本高昂，過程中累積的大量痕跡、反思與評估結果在最佳化結束後多半被丟棄。作者提出 Turbo Harness，將外層搜尋產生的「廢氣」回收再利用：先依 ACE 式流程把搜尋檔案整理成結構化 playbook，記錄有效與無效的編輯策略及其適用條件；再以 GRPO 訓練一個輕量的 harness editor（實驗中用 Qwen3.5-9B），讓它在推論時只依據實例、全域外殼程式碼與 playbook 產生一份補丁，將全域外殼改寫成該實例專屬版本，交由凍結的執行模型運行。實驗涵蓋 ALFWorld、ScienceWorld、DBBench、WebShop、SWE-smith-MR、SWE-bench Verified 與 Terminal-Bench-2.1 共七個基準；在四個代理任務上平均由 Meta-Harness 的 50.2 提升至 56.1，SWE-smith-MR 搭配 Gemini 由 70.7% 升至 88.0%，且每題步數由 23.1 降至 8.7、成本由 0.310 降至 0.046 美元；在 TB2.1 上取得 55.5% 的最高通過率，同時降低回合數與成本。消融顯示 RL 與 playbook 缺一不可：未訓練的 9B 編輯器即使取得 playbook 僅得 50.0%，兩者結合才達 64.0%，並可媲美以 Opus-4.6 擔任編輯器的表現。限制在於方法依賴既有全域搜尋的品質與多樣性，且訓練編輯器仍需額外環境 rollout，在代理任務上成本不低。
papers.title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization
papers.title_zh: Turbo Harness：實例自適應的代理執行外殼最佳化

links.title: Fyan: A Human--AI Harness with Semantic Auditing for Document-Level Formalization

evidence: Abstract: with the same model (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) in every stage, Fyan proves 86 of 143 FormalTCS theorems under a strict Lean check, against 69 for a general agent harness

Section 2.2, Figure 2: an LLM proposes the comparison evidence, while deterministic code checks coverage, scope, polarity, and admissible transfer directions and computes the grade (min_i s_i, non-compensatory)
Section 2.3: a grade 1 statement is admitted only with a Lean bridge obligation S1 -> S0; Appendix E.2 Theorem E.1 gives the scope-preserving compositional transfer proof
Section 3.3, Table 3: semantic audit recall 0.777 vs 0.636 direct judge on verified labels; Appendix C.2 reports exact McNemar p=0.027 and 95% bootstrap intervals
Section 4 Limitations: one model and one trajectory per item, ODENumLib covers a single domain, no ablation of Curator and Orchestrator supervision yet

Reproducibility statement: repository https://anonymous.4open.science/r/fyan-release-78C6 with implementation, prompts, configurations; Appendix G.1 Table 14 lists semantic-audit defaults and Appendix G.2 reproduces the Judge prompt verbatim
Appendix B.2: Formalizer-only run on ProofNet# solves 216 of 343 statements (63.0%) under strict verification, reported only as an absolute cross-corpus evaluation
Appendix C.2: verified labels re-screened blind by Claude Opus 5.5 then author-confirmed; 10 remaining audit false alarms attributed to implementation failures
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strongly on-preference: an LLM-driven agentic harness (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) for formal theorem proving, combining agents/tool use, mathematical reasoning, and code generation across several high-weight preferences. Core novelty is the evidence-grounded semantic audit: an LLM proposes structured slot-level evidence while a deterministic validator computes a non-compensatory minimum grade, plus Lean-checked proof-transfer/bridge obligations (Section 2.2-2.3, Theorem E.1) - a genuinely new acceptance discipline beyond direct LLM judging or BEq+ provability. Evaluation is solid but bounded: controlled FormalTCS comparison (86/143 vs 69/143 under strict Lean check), ConsistencyCheck audit vs direct judge with bootstrap CIs and McNemar p=0.027, and an ODENumLib case study. Weaknesses: single model, one trajectory per item, no ablations of Curator/Orchestrator supervision (admitted in Section 4), single-domain document case study, and label re-verification partially relies on model screening plus author confirmation, which weakens the verified-label comparison slightly. Claims are carefully scoped (fail-closed gates, honest reporting of false alarms and costs), and reproducibility is strong with a released repository, pinned Lean/Mathlib revisions, configuration tables, and verbatim prompts (Appendices G, B).

primary_link.title: Fyan: A Human--AI Harness with Semantic Auditing for Document-Level Formalization

papers.summary: We present FYAN, a human--AI harness for document-level mathematical formalization. Rather than treating theorems in isolation, FYAN coordinates an end-to-end workflow spanning specification, proof planning, logical review, Lean proof construction, knowledge curation, and validation, with support for independent supervision and human guidance. A central component is evidence-grounded semantic auditing, which assesses whether formal statements faithfully preserve their informal specifications. A
papers.summary_zh: 這篇論文處理一個長期被忽略的問題：Lean 等證明助理只檢查形式命題是否可證，卻不檢查形式命題是否忠實對應原文。在文件層級形式化中，一旦某個被改動過的敘述被下游定理重複引用，錯誤會沿相依鏈無聲擴散。作者提出 Fyan，一套人機協作框架，將規格擷取、證明規劃、邏輯審查、Lean 證明建構、知識淬鍊與驗證串成端到端流程，並以文件級相依 DAG 決定形式化順序。其核心是證據導向的語意稽核：由語言模型提出局部對應、遺漏、範圍與邏輯關係等結構化證據，再由決定性驗證程式檢查覆蓋率、極性與容許的轉移方向，並以非補償性的最小值給定等級；只有對齊顯然可見的敘述可直接凍結，被允許的實質偏離則須以 Lean 檢驗的橋接義務把候選敘述接回面向原始規格的敘述。實驗在模型、工具鏈與評分器固定的條件下進行：同為 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash，Fyan 在 143 條 FormalTCS 定理中通過 86 條嚴格 Lean 檢查，對照組為 69 條；自然語言證明分數由 0.501 提升至 0.851。在 ConsistencyCheck 上，其稽核在重驗標籤下的召回率為 0.777（直接判斷為 0.636），原始標籤下為 0.873（0.820），且能定位出錯的假設、結論或範圍。作者亦建構 ODENumLib，共 20 個相依單元、9,355 行 Lean 的常微分方程數值分析程式庫。限制在於僅使用單一模型與單一軌跡、案例涵蓋單一領域、每條敘述的稽核成本明顯高於單次判斷，且部分轉換仍待機械化檢查。其意義在於把「證明能力」與「語意忠實性」明確分離，為可重用形式化函式庫提供可重現的接受標準。
papers.title: Fyan: A Human--AI Harness with Semantic Auditing for Document-Level Formalization
papers.title_zh: Fyan：結合語意稽核的文件級數學形式化人機協作框架

links.title: SEW: Style-Encoded Watermarking of LLM-Generated Code

evidence: Abstract: 'SEW achieves a mean relative improvement of 12.44% in TPR@FPR5% over the baselines and is robust to four non-LLM code-editing attacks, with only a 0.94% mean relative decrease.'
Table 3 / Section 5.1: 'SEW achieved the highest TPR@FPR5% in all nine settings, ranging from 96.60% to 100%, with a mean of 99.14%' and 'pass@1 exactly matching Vanilla in all nine settings.'
Table 4 / Section 5.2: under LLM rewriting SEW TPR@FPR5% '52.55%-99.02%, averaging 74.79%, but SEW remained highest in all nine settings' while 'ACW reached 0% in all three Python settings.'

Table 6 / Section 5.5: calibration raises Atk. 'from 73.14%-73.58% to 82.38%-91.15%'; combined config achieves highest Atk. '97.18%-99.00%' and Flip '77.49%-88.00%'; also admits combined 'matches grade-level detection alone in all nine' for T@5.
Table 5 / Section 5.4: rule-inference accuracy at N=10 'baselines... reaching 85.97%-99.67% accuracy, whereas SEW achieved 19.91%'; SEW rises to 45.17% at N=100.
Appendix F: over ten random 128-bit keys, mean TPR@FPR5% 'ranged from 96.60% to 100%' with setting-level std between 0.00 and 0.81.

Appendix H (Limitations): 'Very short programs can contain too few eligible style sites for reliable watermark detection' and 'Incomplete or structurally invalid outputs can prevent site identification.'
Appendix A: calibration corpus '11,834 Python, 10,643 Java, and 11,594 C++ files'; greedy decoding with 8,192 max tokens; code 'available at https://github.com/suhanmen/SEW' (Abstract).

Table 3: baseline anomaly - STA-1 on gemma-4 Python reports TPR@FPR5% 7.10 with AUROC 33.89 (below random), and STONE reaches only 6.12-45.00 T@5, suggesting possible baseline misconfiguration despite claimed recommended configurations (Section 4.2).
Appendix B / Table 7: per-setting problem counts after filtering are 140-233, indicating small evaluation sets for FPR5% estimation.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Post-hoc watermarking of LLM-generated code is squarely in-scope: it serves AI Safety (provenance, adversarial robustness, detection), Code & Programming, and LLM topics, with no excluded-domain content. Methodological contribution is solid but incremental over existing post-hoc style/transform watermarking (ACW, SrcMarker, RoSeMary); the genuinely new pieces are style-preference calibration against natural style frequencies (Section 3.1), grade-level aggregation preventing evidence inflation (Section 3.3), and key+context-conditioned target assignment via HMAC-SHA256 for pattern resistance (Section 3.2). Rigor is strong: 9 model-language settings, 8 baselines, 5 code-editing attacks plus targeted style-flipping and rule-inference attacks, component ablations (Table 6), and key-sensitivity analysis (Appendix F). Weaknesses: small per-setting test sets (Table 7: 140-233 problems) make TPR@FPR5% noisy; several baselines show below-random scores (e.g., STA-1 7.10 TPR / 33.89 AUROC on gemma-4 Python, Table 3) hinting at possible baseline misconfiguration; the independent-grades assumption in the statistical test (Section 3.3) is unexamined; and evaluation is confined to CodeContests competitive-programming code, limiting generalizability to real-world codebases and new languages (hand-crafted 29/22/19 rules). Evidence is extensive and internally consistent, including the honest report that calibration adds no T@5 gain over grade-level detection alone (Section 5.5) and acknowledged limitations for short/invalid code (Appendix H). Reproducibility is good: code link, full rule list (Appendix I), calibration corpus sizes and timing (Appendix C), baseline training details (Appendix A).

primary_link.title: SEW: Style-Encoded Watermarking of LLM-Generated Code

papers.summary: Code watermarking supports provenance tracking for code generated by LLMs. Modifying token selection to embed watermarks as an LLM generates code can create a trade-off between detectability and functional correctness. Other methods instead watermark completed code using predefined transformations or trained neural models. Recurring patterns can make watermark choices predictable across programs, while treating patterns common in unwatermarked code as watermark evidence can cause false detection
papers.summary_zh: 這篇論文針對「如何驗證 LLM 生成程式碼的來源」提出一套後置式（post-hoc）浮水印方法 SEW（Style-Encoded Watermarking）。既有做法可分兩類：一類在解碼階段改動 token 選擇，容易在低熵程式碼中犧牲功能正確性；另一類對已完成程式碼套用固定轉換或訓練式神經抽取模型，其固定或反覆出現的風格決策可被攻擊者跨程式推斷，而自然就常見的風格又可能造成誤判。SEW 由三個元件組成：一是從風格指南與既有程式轉換規則建構的二元風格規則庫（Python 29 條、Java 22 條、C++ 19 條），依密鑰與程式的結構脈絡決定每個可套用位置的風格變體；二是風格偏好校準，利用人類撰寫程式碼估計各變體的自然機率，避免把本來就常見的風格當成浮水印證據；三是脈絡感知風格聚合，將具有相同結構識別碼與程式脈絡的位置併為一個 grade，以多數值代表，防止同一風格決策被重複計數而膨脹證據。偵測時不需生成模型、不需參考原始碼，也不需嵌入中介資料。實驗在 CodeContests 上以三種 LLM（Qwen3.5-9B、gemma-4-12B-it、gpt-oss-20b）與三種語言（Python、Java、C++）共九個設定進行，平均 TPR@FPR5% 達 99.14%，相對最強基線平均提升 12.44%，且 pass@1 與未加浮水印版本完全一致。面對四種非 LLM 的程式編輯攻擊（排版、預設 lint、註解移除、識別碼改名），TPR 平均僅相對下降 0.94%；在 LLM 改寫攻擊下仍維持最高偵測率，但降至 52.55%–99.02%，顯示對結構性改寫僅具部分穩健性。此外，規則推論實驗中 SEW 的決策可預測性明顯低於基線。限制在於：極短程式可用的合格風格位置過少，且無法解析的不完整或結構無效程式會降低覆蓋率；這些皆屬輸入本身的缺陷，而非嵌入所造成。此方法的重要性在於提供免訓練、免解碼存取、兼顧功能正確性與抗模式推斷的程式碼溯源機制。
papers.title: SEW: Style-Encoded Watermarking of LLM-Generated Code
papers.title_zh: SEW：針對 LLM 生成程式碼的風格編碼浮水印

links.title: Thinking Outside the Box: Can Language Models Rely on External Guidance Selectively?

evidence: Abstract: introduces Box2-Bench holding model/task fixed while varying workflow reliability across five matched conditions, and trains two open-weight models with counterfactual SFT and outcome-based RL on bad workflows.

Section 2.3, Table 1: bad workflows reduce performance in all twelve frontier model-task pairs (drops 2.3-43.3 points) while good workflows improve 8/12 pairs, supporting the utilization-vs-robustness gap claim.
Section 3.2, Table 3: SFT shrinks the AIME bad-workflow penalty from 20.0 to 6.7 points and WebShop from 9.8 to 0.6; RL restores AIME utilization (delta_use) from -3.3 to +6.7.
Appendix A.2: evaluation uses all 30 AIME 2026 problems with 8 samples per condition via majority voting and 500 official WebShop test tasks, with no evaluation instance used in training.

Appendix C.2: workflow acceptance relies on a model-based semantic reviewer (gpt-5.6-sol); the authors state they 'report neither an inter-annotator reliability coefficient nor a candidate-level rejection rate.'

Section 4, Figure 6: EoM multi-agent transfer uses 30 problems x 5 episodes (150 total); SFT raises success from 18.00% to 22.67% while SFT+RL reaches 18.67%, with the paper noting 'gains are not monotonic across training stages.'

Appendix D.1 and Table 4: memory transfer uses 30 of 387 LongMemEval-V2-Small questions with 3 rollouts; accuracy moves 21.1% (base) to 28.9% (SFT), a difference of roughly 2-3 questions without reported variance.
Appendix B.2: relative-reward RL ablation reports 'Neither RL reward consistently dominates,' isolating the reward-design choice from the SFT checkpoint.

Appendix A ('Released resources'): 'Box2-Bench and the trained model checkpoints are publicly available through our Hugging Face collection,' supporting reproducibility, though optimizer hyperparameters are not specified in the text.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-agent reasoning/reliability work: a benchmark (Box2-Bench) that holds task and model fixed while varying workflow reliability across five matched conditions, plus a training study (counterfactual SFT on bad workflows, then outcome-based GRPO RL) with transfer to multi-agent and memory settings. Strongly aligned with high-weight preferences (LLMs, agents/tool use, reasoning, safety-robustness, training/RL). Novelty is solid: isolating selective reliance on fallible guidance, including Partial-vs-Mixed recovery effects, is a fresh angle beyond task-completion or compliance benchmarks. Rigor is good in design (matched paired effects, scale sweeps across Qwen3/Qwen3.5 sizes, RL reward ablation, strict train/test task separation) but weakened by small samples (30 AIME problems with 8-sample majority voting; 30-item memory subset; 150 EoM episodes), no confidence intervals or significance tests, and workflow verification done solely by LLM review with no human annotation or rejection-rate reporting (acknowledged in Appendix C.2). Evidence strength is moderate: extensive condition-level tables, but headline transfer gains are thin (EoM SFT+RL 18.67% vs base 18.00%; memory 21.1%->28.9% on 30 questions, ~2-3 items) and the authors concede non-monotonic gains. Generalizability is supported by four frontier task domains and two transfer settings, though workflows come from one fixed generator and one training recipe. Reproducibility is aided by a claimed Hugging Face release of bench and checkpoints, seeds, and detailed protocols, but training hyperparameters and full prompts are only partially given.

primary_link.title: Thinking Outside the Box: Can Language Models Rely on External Guidance Selectively?

papers.summary: Agent harnesses often improve language models with human-designed workflows, but as models grow more capable, unreliable guidance can increasingly constrain their execution. We call the ability to benefit from useful guidance while overriding unreliable guidance thinking outside the box. We introduce Box$^2$-Bench, which holds the model and task fixed while varying workflow reliability to isolate how models regulate their reliance on guidance. On Box$^2$-Bench, frontier models often benefit from
papers.summary_zh: 這篇論文指出，現今的大型語言模型多半在人類設計的工作流程（workflow）框架下運作，但當模型自身能力提升後，不可靠的流程反而可能限制其表現。作者將「有益時遵循外部程序指引、誤導時加以抗拒、出現更佳策略時予以超越」的能力稱為 thinking outside the box，並提出 Box²-Bench。此基準固定模型、任務、環境與評估器，只變動工作流程的可用性與可靠性，設計出無流程、Good、Partial、Mixed、Bad 五種配對條件，並以固定的外部模型作為可規模化的流程設計者代理，所有流程皆經獨立驗證器檢查有效性與答案洩漏後凍結。在 AIME 2026、WebShop、OpenR1-Math、DeepSWE、BrowseComp、AutomationBench 等任務上，前沿模型與開源權重模型普遍能從良好流程受益，卻在流程具誤導性或中途轉為不可靠時明顯受損；Mixed 條件在十二組前沿模型中就有十組低於對應的 Partial，顯示模型對初期有效流程產生依賴慣性，難以隨可靠性變化即時修正。作者進一步以僅含 Bad 流程的資料訓練開源模型：反事實監督式微調（SFT）能提升對錯誤指引的穩健性，但會過度抗拒流程；接續以任務結果為基礎的強化學習（GRPO）則可部分恢復對未見良好流程的使用，並改善指引中止或轉為誤導時的復原。研究亦發現此選擇性依賴可初步遷移至多代理協作中的同儕修正，以及記憶增強推理中對損毀記憶的查核行為。限制在於流程由固定模型生成、可靠性變化受控且凍結，尚未涵蓋互動式、模糊、部分正確或可隨模型調整的指引，也未估計人類撰寫流程中錯誤的自然分布。其意義在於指出選擇性依賴是代理可靠性中未被任務表現單一指標捕捉的獨立面向。
papers.title: Thinking Outside the Box: Can Language Models Rely on External Guidance Selectively?
papers.title_zh: 跳脫框架思考：語言模型能否選擇性地依賴外部指引？

links.title: Debias It Yourself: Teaching LLMs Cognitive Bias Mitigation Interventions

evidence: Abstract: 'Train+Revise and Revise alone attain the top two average ranks... reduce bias on unseen dimensions by up to 14.8%'
Section 5.1, Takeaway 1: 'On every tested model, the best average rank across bias benchmarks is achieved by a DIY configuration, with intervention-guided revision in the top two on every model'
Table 19 (Appendix H): paired bootstrap 95% CIs, e.g., Llama-8B DIY-Train-Revise on CrowS-Pairs +14.98 [+11.22,+17.26], but DIY-Show 0 is -2.34 [-5.07,+0.49] on CrowS-Pairs

Table 21 (Appendix H): DIY-Show 1 attains 0.000 on both BBQ subsets for all three models, and baselines show degenerate values (DPO BBQ-Disambig 35.475; DebiasNLG CrowS-Pairs 9.42; BiasEdit StereoSet 0.000 on Llama-70B), undermining clean baseline comparison

Section 3.2 / Appendix C: 4,500 seed rows expanded to 67,500 biased-debiased pairs generated by Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct; Table 14 reports LLM-as-judge validation of 1,000 pairs with acceptance 89.8-99.2%
Limitations: 'Artifacts of the prompting model may propagate into the data' and 'We cannot directly verify whether the model's underlying processing of social cues has changed'
Appendix I: 'The available training-based Regard generations used an earlier LoRA specification and are therefore excluded' - artifact inconsistency in open-ended evaluation

Appendix G Table 17 and Section 4: full LoRA configuration (r=64, alpha=128, lr 2e-4, 4-bit NF4, fixed 500+100 example budget, 90 optimization steps) with no hyperparameter sweep; GitHub link in Section 1 footnote
Section 5.3 / Figure 7: gender-source training transfers to unseen dimensions with positive reduction; Appendix J extends source-dimension analysis across three models
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM safety/fairness research (LLMs, prompting/ICL, instruction tuning, reasoning preservation, bias benchmarks), squarely in scope. The framework systematically translates five psychology-validated interventions into Show/Train/Revise paradigms, but each ingredient (self-debiasing, moral self-correction, contact-hypothesis and perspective-taking debiasing) exists in prior work, so novelty is a solid-but-incremental synthesis. Evaluation is unusually broad: 3 models, 5 bias + 3 reasoning benchmarks, 11 reimplemented baselines, paired bootstrap CIs, ablations, and cross-dimension transfer. Evidence is weakened by anomalies: DIY-Show 1-shot attains exactly 0.000 BBQ scores on all three models (Table 21), several baselines show degenerate values (DPO 35.475 BBQ-Disambig, DebiasNLG 9.42 CrowS-Pairs) suggesting failed reimplementations that may inflate DIY's relative standing, and Regard results exclude training-based conditions due to an earlier LoRA specification (Appendix I). Synthetic data is generated by Llama-3.3-70B, a model also evaluated, acknowledged as a circularity risk in Limitations. Honest limitations on output-vs-internal-processing and benchmark-shaped scoring. Strong reproducibility: public code/data, full hyperparameters (Table 17), and prompt templates. Overall a well-executed, relevant paper whose headline comparisons deserve some caution.

primary_link.title: Debias It Yourself: Teaching LLMs Cognitive Bias Mitigation Interventions

papers.summary: Bias has long been studied in social psychology and cognitive science, where decades of research have produced a body of validated interventions that reduce stereotypical thinking and prejudiced responses in humans. We propose Debias It Yourself (DIY), a cognitively grounded framework that translates five such interventions into debiasing procedures for large language models and delivers them through three established paradigms: Show (in-context examples), Train (instruction tuning), and Revise
papers.summary_zh: 這篇論文把社會心理學中經過實證驗證的偏見降低介入策略，轉譯成大型語言模型的去偏見程序。作者借用 Devine 等人的「偏見習慣破除」架構，選出五種認知策略：刻板印象替換、反刻板印象想像、個體化、觀點取替與正向接觸，並將每一種拆解成明確的三步驟流程。這些流程透過三種既有學習範式送入模型：Show（脈絡內示範）、Train（指令微調）與 Revise（介入引導的自我修訂），組合成九種 DIY 設定。實驗涵蓋三個模型（Llama-3.1-8B、Llama-3.3-70B、Qwen3.5-27B）、五個偏見基準、十一個既有去偏見基線與三個推理基準。結果顯示，Train+Revise 與 Revise 在每個模型上都取得最佳平均排名，能在約九成推理準確率下把平均偏見壓到約百分之二，並對訓練時未見的偏見面向帶來最高十四點八個百分點的降低。限制方面，訓練資料為合成生成，可能帶有生成模型的偏誤，且研究只觀察基準分數，無法確認模型內部處理是否真正改變，也未評估對話與多跳推理。此工作的重要性在於把 LLM 去偏見從個別基準的臨時修補，轉向以既有偏見理論為依據、可系統推導的方法。
papers.title: Debias It Yourself: Teaching LLMs Cognitive Bias Mitigation Interventions
papers.title_zh: 自己動手去偏見：教導大型語言模型認知偏誤緩解介入策略

links.title: Towards Better Exploration in Sequential Test-Time Scaling

evidence: Abstract: 'Across 27 combinations of scaling methods, models, and benchmarks, we find that 53.8% of sequential scaling trajectories enter an attractor within four iterations' and the intervention 'reduces the attractor hit rate by 21.2 percentage points on average'.

Section 4.2, Table 2: attractor hit-by-S4 rates range 23.3-88.7% across method-model-benchmark combinations; right columns imply at least 7.7% of attractors are suboptimal via paired-trajectory correctness differences.
Section 5.2, Table 3: M_mix lowers attractor hit rates vs GPT OSS 120B (e.g., RSA on IMO 88.7% -> 67.7%, RGG 81.0% -> 49.7%) and lowers suboptimal-attractor probabilities.

Finding 4 and Figure 3 (Section 5.2): sequential scaling with M_mix surpasses both the sequential GPT-only baseline and the compute-matched parallel baseline in coverage 'in almost every case'; abstract claims 3.3pp more correct answers than parallel scaling.
Finding 7 / Appendix J, Figure 13: annealed model sampling improves RSA accuracy by 2.2pp on IMO-AnswerBench and 2.3pp on Reasoning Gym Games at 3.6%/3.4% lower OpenRouter cost.

Appendix G, Table 6: parallel coverage of M_mix alone (82.0/62.8/77.3) is below GPT OSS 120B (82.8/64.5/79.0), supporting that gains come from sequential exploration rather than complementary model capabilities; Appendix H shows temperature increases do not explain the gains.

Appendix K, Table 7 and Figures 14-15: on ARC AGI 1 the single-model baseline outperforms M_mix, an honest negative result with a hypothesis (non-verifiable objectives yield fewer suboptimal attractors).
Appendix B.3: GPT OSS 20B grader matches Gemini 2.5 Pro on 99.25% of 2,000 sampled answers, with only 17 grading disagreements when re-checking changed problems.

Appendix B.4.3, Table 4: attractor hit-rate sensitivity across attractor-identification seeds is small (standard deviations 0.33-3.83pp), and Figure 6 validates that progress flattens after attractor entry.

Reproducibility Statement and abstract footnote: code at anonymous.4open.science/r/tts-exploration; Appendix B details setup, prompts, model configurations, and grading; Section 6 acknowledges limited configurations and no frontier models, and Appendix A excludes tools, latent-space, and gradient-based test-time methods.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A core LLM reasoning / test-time scaling paper that squarely matches high-weight preferences (LLMs, reasoning & CoT, test-time compute, inference). The contribution is a dynamical-systems framing of sequential scaling (states, transitions, attractor definition), systematic quantification of premature convergence to suboptimal attractors across 27 method-model-benchmark combinations, and a simple model-mixing intervention. Novelty is moderate: the paper itself cites roughly ten prior works observing attractor-like convergence in specific settings, and model mixing has known mixed results (Section 2.3); the value lies in unification, compute-matched coverage comparisons, and the negative-result boundary analysis, not a fundamentally new method. Rigor is solid: formal Definition 4.1, compute-matched parallel baselines, temperature and tree-of-thoughts controls, mixture-concentration ablations, seed-sensitivity analysis, grader validation, and an honest failure case on ARC AGI 1; weakened by heuristic attractor identification (KMeans over embeddings with several hand-set thresholds), transition estimation from only three trajectories per configuration, and some single-seed ablations. Evidence is quantitative and internally consistent, though effect sizes are modest (2.2pp accuracy; 21.2pp attractor-hit reduction). Generalizability is reasonable within verifiable maths/game reasoning, with transfer tested to Qwen3 235B, but scope excludes tools, latent/gradient methods, and frontier models. Reproducibility is supported by an anonymous code link and a detailed experimental appendix.
topics: exploration and diversity in LLM search

primary_link.title: Towards Better Exploration in Sequential Test-Time Scaling

papers.summary: Test-time scaling improves language model reasoning by spending additional compute at inference. However, both classes of existing methods often fail to continue improving over long timescales. Parallel methods repeatedly sample independent answers from the model, scaling poorly on problems the model is unlikely to solve in a single attempt. In contrast, sequential methods build on previous answers to access new ideas, yet so far have not been shown to reach answers beyond those found by paralle
papers.summary_zh: 這篇論文探討測試時擴展（test-time scaling）為何在長時間尺度下停止進步。作者將測試時擴展方法統一表述為動態系統，並提出「吸引子」（attractor）概念：一旦進入某組答案，方法便難以跳脫。在 27 組序列式擴展方法、模型與基準的組合中，平均 53.8% 的軌跡在前四次迭代內即陷入吸引子；若兩條同設定軌跡都落入吸引子，約 15.4% 的情況其中一個只含錯誤答案，顯示至少 7.7% 的吸引子屬次優，若能逃脫即可提升準確率。作者提出的介入方式很簡單：隨機在多個語言模型間切換（M_mix），使一個模型的吸引子未必是另一個模型的吸引子。此舉平均降低 21.2 個百分點的吸引子命中率，讓序列式方法的覆蓋率超越同算力的平行式基線，並在遞迴自聚合（RSA）上至少提升 2.2 個百分點的準確率。作者也發現混合比例以偏向主模型（c=0.75）最佳，並以退火式取樣兼顧探索與利用。限制在於實驗僅涵蓋有限設定與非前沿模型，ARC AGI 1 上因無明確驗證目標、吸引子較少，基線反而較佳。此工作主張長時程測試時擴展應由平行式搜尋轉向能改進既有答案的序列式學習過程。
papers.title: Towards Better Exploration in Sequential Test-Time Scaling
papers.title_zh: 改善序列式測試時擴展的探索能力：逃離次優吸引子

links.title: From Imitation to Reward Discovery: On-Policy Warmup for Agentic RL

evidence: Abstract — identifies an 'On-Policy Acceleration Phenomenon' and proposes OPW: teacher supervision on the student's own interaction trajectories before teacher-free RLVR.
Section 4.2 / Table 2 — ALFWorld Unseen final success 96.7% (OPW+GRPO) vs 86.6% (direct GRPO) and 53.5% (direct OPD); ScienceWorld Unseen 68.2 vs 61.2 vs 55.2.

Section 3.1 & Appendix A — Proposition 3.1 (trajectory KL equals population OPD loss) and Theorem 3.2 (success transfer via data-processing inequality and Pinsker), with complete proofs; assumptions explicitly scoped (population loss, shared environment).
Section 4.1 — students Qwen3-1.7B/4B, teacher Qwen3-32B; baselines off-policy SFT, SFT-RS, teacher-free GRPO warmup; 40 warmup + 60 GRPO steps.
Section 5 / Appendix D.3 & Table 18 — targeted removal of supervision at repeated invalid actions lowers early GRPO gain (34.6 vs 41.5 pp Seen), isolating a mechanism behind the acceleration.

Appendix C.3 / Table 15 — recorded training cost including teacher scoring: OPW 27.3 vs GRPO-warmup 29.6 GPU-hours at 4B, but higher at 1.7B (23.9 vs 22.2), honestly distinguishing faster learning from lower total cost.
Section 5 (Task-Specific Performance) — concedes OPW does not lead the ScienceWorld Mixing category, showing gains are not uniform.
Appendix C.2 / Table 14 — two-seed replication of the OPW vs GRPO-warmup comparison with consistent direction.
Appendix I — limitations acknowledged: only ALFWorld and ScienceWorld testbeds; no code/data release stated anywhere in the document.
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM training-methodology paper: teacher-guided on-policy distillation warmup (OPW) before GRPO-style RLVR for language-model agents on Qwen3 students (1.7B/4B) with a 32B teacher. Strongly matches Agents & Tool Use, LLM, RL, and Training preferences; not an out-of-scope domain application. Novelty is moderate: OPD-as-warmup-then-RL is very close to concurrent works the paper itself tabulates (OPDSearch+, Sequential Beats Joint, RL Starts before RL); the distinctive part is the trajectory-KL/reward-discovery theory and the error-state supervision analysis, and the theory (data-processing inequality + Pinsker) is elementary though correctly derived. Rigor is high: clear assumption scoping, five baselines/paths, ablations (targeted vs random supervision removal, fixed vs resampled trajectories, warmup durations, two seeds), unbiased pass@k/pass^k estimators, and cost accounting that includes teacher scoring and honestly reports higher cost at 1.7B. Evidence is solid within its scope but limited to two text-game environments, one model family, one teacher, and no confidence intervals on the headline comparisons. Reproducibility documentation is unusually detailed (hyperparameters, seeds, token counts, partitions) but no code or data release is stated.

primary_link.title: From Imitation to Reward Discovery: On-Policy Warmup for Agentic RL

papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with a verifiable reward (RLVR) offers a scalable approach to training language-model agents, yet sparse outcome rewards can leave early training with little signal for policy improvement. We identify an On-Policy Acceleration Phenomenon: in our main comparisons, RLVR initialized with on-policy distillation reaches high performance earlier in training and achieves both higher average performance during subsequent RLVR and higher final performance than the alternative basel
papers.summary_zh: 這篇論文探討可驗證獎勵強化學習（RLVR）在代理任務上的冷啟動問題：當成功需要多個決策協同配合時，初始策略往往產生大量失敗軌跡，二元結果獎勵下同組全數失敗會讓 GRPO 等群組相對方法缺乏組內對比訊號。作者觀察到「同期策略加速現象」——以同期策略蒸餾暖身後再進行 RLVR，會更早達到高效能，且後續 RLVR 期間的平均與最終表現都優於基線。據此提出 On-Policy Warmup（OPW）：學生先在自身與環境互動產生的軌跡上接受固定教師的監督，包含不完美動作與復原情境，之後才切換到無需教師查詢的 RLVR。理論上，作者證明在共用環境動態下，學生造訪狀態上的累積反向 KL 蒸餾損失等於學生與教師軌跡分布的 KL 散度，再透過資料處理不等式推得初始驗證器成功率的下界，以及獎勵探索複雜度的上界；對群組相對 RLVR 亦刻畫成功率上升如何提高出現「有成功也有失敗」之獎勵資訊性群組的機率。實驗在 ALFWorld 與 ScienceWorld 上以 Qwen3-1.7B／4B 為學生、Qwen3-32B 為教師，OPW 在最終任務表現與重複任務成功（pass^8）上多數優於 off-policy SFT、SFT-RS 與無教師 GRPO 暖身，並大幅減少重複無效動作。限制在於理論只保證初始獎勵探索，不保證收斂或整體算力更省；暖身長度與端到端效率需依任務與教師成本調整，且增益在 ScienceWorld 部分類別並不均勻。
papers.title: From Imitation to Reward Discovery: On-Policy Warmup for Agentic RL
papers.title_zh: 從模仿到獎勵探索：代理式強化學習的同期策略暖身

links.title: LatentHarness: Learning Latent Actions for Memory and Reasoning via Counterfactual Policy Distillation

evidence: Table 1 (Section 3): at 1.4B, long-context averages LatentHarness 49.7 vs Memory-R2 45.2, latency 3.0s vs 17.7s (supports the 5.9x claim), FLOPs 48% vs 391%.
Abstract: claims 2.8% and 10.0% relative improvements at 1.4B; arithmetic verified against Table 1 family averages (55.8 vs 54.3; 49.7 vs 45.2).

Section 3.2 RQ1, Table 2: GRPO-only ablation loses 5.4 long-context points (44.3); VinePPO branches reach 48.6 at 3.6x training compute vs 49.7 at 1.1x; policy entropy 0.21 (GRPO) vs 0.68 nats (ours).
Section 3.2 RQ3, Table 3: evidence-recall hit rate 63.9% vs 0.5% chance at 64k tokens; MuSiQue F1 falls 42.1 (2-hop) to 16.4 (4-hop); distractor outranks supporting passage in 72% of 3+-hop errors.

Section 2.2, Eqs. 7-10: one-step counterfactual branches define action gains G(a|s); Eq. 10 write-gate credit is acknowledged as a partial derivative that 'ignores how a gate would alter later keys, values, gates, queries, and actions.'

Section 3 (Datasets/Baselines): all trained methods share the same backbone, training data, and RL step count; OOD suites (GPQA-Diamond, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue) padded to 64k, exceeding all training lengths.

Whole document: no seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests reported; no code or artifact release statement; numeric values for the action cost rho, c_R, loss weights (beta, gamma, lambda, eta), and CPD temperature are not specified.
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM methodology paper unifying latent reasoning and memory access as a Think/Recall/Exit latent action policy over a fast-weight delta-rule memory, trained with a new counterfactual policy distillation objective on top of GRPO. Strongly matches high-weight preferences (LLMs, reasoning, long-context/memory, RL training). The integration is novel, but it composes known parts (looped backbones/Ouro, fast weights, GRPO, VinePPO-style branching, policy distillation). Rigor is solid: two backbone scales, six suites with OOD splits, budget-matched baselines, and ablations over credit assignment, action space, gate targets, and action cost; headline numbers are internally consistent (55.8 vs 54.3 = +2.8% relative; 49.7 vs 45.2 = +10.0%; 3.0s vs 17.7s = 5.9x). Docked for single-run results with no variance or significance reporting, evaluation limited to QA-style tasks despite agent-motivated framing, no code/artifact release, and unstated key hyperparameters (rho, c_R, loss weights, CPD temperature).

primary_link.title: LatentHarness: Learning Latent Actions for Memory and Reasoning via Counterfactual Policy Distillation

papers.summary: Long-context reasoning faces two complementary bottlenecks: retaining evidence across long inputs and sustaining computation across many reasoning steps. Existing approaches largely address them separately, with external memory extending access to distant evidence and latent reasoning compressing multi-step computation. We introduce LatentHarness, which unifies memory access and latent reasoning as sequential latent action selection. At each internal step, the model chooses THINK for further com
papers.summary_zh: 長脈絡推理同時面臨兩種長度瓶頸：一是證據分散在長輸入中，難以保留；二是解題需要大量中間推理步驟。既有做法多半各自處理其中一種：外部記憶代理把遙遠證據留在模型之外，再透過上下文視窗讀回；潛在推理方法則把中間計算從解碼文字搬進內部表徵。本文提出 LatentHarness，把記憶存取與潛在推理統一為序列式潛在動作選擇：每個內部步驟中，潛在策略在 Think（再算一步並寫入 fast-weight 記憶）、Recall（從同時存放輸入證據與中間推理狀態的記憶讀取）與 Exit（輸出下一個 token）之間選擇。由於軌跡層級獎勵對個別潛在決策的信用分配過於粗略，作者提出反事實策略蒸餾（CPD）：在每個潛在狀態對每個允許動作分支一步，量測其對輸出 token 對數機率的改變，得到動作增益；這些增益一方面作為狀態層級動作信用教導策略，另一方面透過記憶微分，以正優勢軌跡上後續 Recall 的變化來監督寫入閘門該保留哪些推導狀態。在以 Ouro-1.4B-Thinking 與 2.6B-Thinking 為骨幹的六個一般與長脈絡推理基準上，1.4B 模型相對最強基線分別提升 2.8% 與 10.0%（相對值），六項平均較 Memory-R2 高 3.9 與 4.1 分，且僅用約 55% 的全深度計算量，長脈絡推理較 Memory-R2 快 5.9 倍。消融顯示移除 CPD 會使策略熵在 200 步內崩落，移除 Recall 或改為每次都讀取皆顯著下降；錯誤分析指出剩餘多跳錯誤主要來自記憶定址，干擾段落常壓過支持段落。此工作的重要處在於把記憶與推理原生地放進同一條潛在計算軌跡，並提供不隨策略收斂而消失的信用分配機制，但目前仍受限於骨幹規模、訓練分布與檢索定址能力，尚未驗證於更大模型或真實代理環境。
papers.title: LatentHarness: Learning Latent Actions for Memory and Reasoning via Counterfactual Policy Distillation
papers.title_zh: LatentHarness：透過反事實策略蒸餾學習用於記憶與推理的潛在動作

links.title: RankEvolve: A Reliable Multi-Agent Auto-Research Harness for Evolving Ranking Models

evidence: Abstract/Section 4.1: cross-checking lifts all-oracle execution accuracy from best single-product 45.8% to 62.5%; paired +16.7, 95% CI [6.6,26.7], p<0.001, twenty discordant tasks (eighteen rescued vs two broken).

Section 4 (Corpus, oracle, and conditions): 96 private tasks per repository with locked snapshots, hidden executable oracles, frozen resource envelope B; six conditions including one-pass, extended-budget, blind best-of-N, and homogeneous CC→CC→CC controls.
Section 4.1 (Transfer): LitGPT forward pair 56.2% vs 43.8%, paired +12.5, CI [3.0,22.0], p=0.008, reported as pre-specified regardless of outcome.

Section 4.2: plan-merge contrast +8.3, exact McNemar p=0.077, CI [-0.7,17.3], explicitly not statistically distinguishable; budget-capped variant ties CC→Codex→CC at 62.5% (paired 0.0, CI [-5.5,5.5]).

Section 4.3/Table 11: runtime-controlled context-scope ablation shows paired EA +2.1 early, +6.2 middle, +10.4 late, with lower CDR and ~4.9k fewer input tokens — mechanism evidence for current-step injection.

Section 5 and Table 5: paper explicitly disclaims novelty for state machines, agents-as-graphs, workflow optimization, checkpointing, and multi-agent debate, claiming only the product-agent adapter boundary and measured reliability.

Table 1 note (Section 3.1): NDCG@10 values are 'reported historical endpoints (best checkpoints, not independent seeds)', and Section 3.3 marks ML-32M baselines as internal reproductions, not published baselines.

Limitations: evidence base is 'one ranking codebase plus LitGPT, both Python/PyTorch'; oracles incomplete (mutation testing reduces, not eliminates, false passes); knowledge layer lacks a memory-on/off ablation; case study ran with a human operator at gates so agent vs operator contribution is not separated.

Appendix B (Reproducibility): public HSTU codebase and MovieLens data, configurations tabulated (Table 6), failure-overlap analyzer/leaderboard schema/boost-last-K patch 'will be released', but ExecML hidden oracles and tasks remain private.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Squarely in-scope LLM-agent methodology paper: multi-agent orchestration of black-box coding-agent products (Claude Code, Codex) for ML engineering plus an incident-seeded execution-accuracy benchmark; recommendation is only the application substrate, so the domain-application exclusion does not apply. Novelty is moderate: the paper itself concedes state machines, agents-as-graphs, and workflow composition are established (Section 5, Table 5), locating its delta at the product-adapter boundary and at measuring whether heterogeneous composition buys correctness at matched budget — a real but narrow contribution. Rigor is exceptional: pre-registered decision rules frozen before private runs, a budget envelope B, hidden oracles with leakage controls (Section 4, Appendix C.1), McNemar/task-clustered bootstrap statistics, a pre-specified LitGPT transfer split reported regardless of outcome, an honest non-significant second-stage topology result (Section 4.2, p=0.077), and a runtime-controlled context-scope ablation (Table 11). Evidence is strong for the primary claim (62.5% vs 45.8% EA, paired +16.7, CI [6.6,26.7]; Section 4.1) but rests on only two Python/PyTorch repositories with n=96 tasks each, an internally validated private hidden-oracle benchmark, and case-study endpoints that are best checkpoints, not independent seeds (Table 1 note); no memory-on/off ablation and a human-steered case study weaken attribution. Generalizability and reproducibility are capped by the private ExecML tasks, commercial black-box products, and the admitted cross-domain limits (Limitations).

primary_link.title: RankEvolve: A Reliable Multi-Agent Auto-Research Harness for Evolving Ranking Models

papers.summary: Auto-research agents, LLM systems that propose, implement, train, and evaluate model changes across iterations, promise to automate applied ML's experimental loop. Over long horizons, execution accuracy is a binding constraint: a change can silently leak held-out data, omit normalization, disconnect a gradient, or leave a train/eval flag unwired, invalidating expensive runs and compounding error across iterations. We present RankEvolve, an auto-research framework for evolving generative ranking
papers.summary_zh: 這篇論文針對「自動研究代理」在長時間迭代下的執行可靠性問題。作者指出，LLM 代理在反覆提出、實作、訓練與評估模型改動時，常犯下測試集外洩、漏掉 layer norm、梯度中斷或 train/eval 旗標未接上等隱性缺陷；這類錯誤不但浪費大量 GPU 時間，還會產生錯誤指標，且隨迭代累積而惡化。為此提出 RankEvolve，包含三項設計：一是可執行操作協定（EOP），把工作流程的階段、相依、閘門與分支迴圈一次宣告，編譯成由執行環境強制執行的狀態機；二是 meta-meta-harness，把 Claude Code、Codex 等完整編碼代理產品當成執行圖節點，透過適配器契約互相審查與修補；三是知識層，保存含負面結果的發現與來源脈絡供後續迭代使用。作者在公開 HSTU 推薦模型上部署十二輪迭代，MovieLens-20M LARGE 取得 NDCG@10 0.2192（較已發表基準 +4.48%），BASE 為 0.1948（+2.80%），並記錄了外洩事件。核心實證來自 ExecML 基準：每個 repo 96 個私有任務、隱藏 oracle，在相同可觀測推論預算下，異質配對 CC→Codex→CC 的執行正確率達 62.5%，優於最佳單一產品 45.8%（配對 +16.7，95% CI [6.6,26.7]），同時將沉默性關鍵缺陷率由 35.4% 降至 10.4%；LitGPT 轉移切分亦複現（+12.5，CI [3.0,22.0]）。機制分析顯示錯誤相關性愈低、可救援的互補錯誤質量愈大，實得增益愈高（斜率 0.34，CI [0.12,0.56]）。第二階段的 plan-merge 拓撲雖有最高正確率 70.8%，但與對照差異未達統計顯著（+8.3,p=0.077），且在固定預算下與三階段配對持平，顯示獲益主要來自「使用不同產品」而非特定拓撲。限制包括：證據僅涵蓋 HSTU 與 LitGPT 兩個 Python/PyTorch 程式庫、oracle 無法完全排除偽通過、產品為黑箱而無法比對供應商端 FLOPs、知識層缺乏 on/off 消融、HSTU 個案仍有人類操作者在閘門介入。其意義在於把「組合不同編碼代理是否真的買到正確性」變成可反駁、預先註冊的系統假設，而非僅憑架構圖推論。
papers.title: RankEvolve: A Reliable Multi-Agent Auto-Research Harness for Evolving Ranking Models
papers.title_zh: RankEvolve：用於演化排序模型的可信多代理自動研究框架

links.title: MemCodex: Self-Programming Hierarchical Memory for Language Agents

evidence: Abstract: claims 10.1% relative improvement over strongest adaptive-memory baseline, 3.4x fewer context tokens, 2.1x faster inference
Section 4.1 Main Results / Table 1: MemCodex averages 60.8% with Qwen3.5-27B (+5.6 over MemPro) and 61.1% with GPT-5.4-mini (+3.6), at 2.0k tokens/question vs 6.8k for MemPro
Section 4.2 Ablation (Table 2): hierarchy depth 1-4 layers gives 54.1/56.5/59.0/60.8 avg with flat ~2k tokens; routing channel 60.8/88.4 Rec/2.0k vs content channel 55.4/63.0 Rec/3.9k
Section 2.2 Acceptance test (Eq. 4): child accepted only if token cost non-increasing and accuracy gain passes one-sided exact McNemar test at alpha=0.05
Section 4 RQ4 / Table 4: record-disjoint splits keep a 5.0-point margin over MemPro; MemCodex drops 1.0 point vs 0.4 for all baselines, bounding record-specific overfitting at ~0.6 points
Section 4 RQ6 / Figure 5 (right): native evolved architectures beat transferred ones by 1.5-2.8 points, showing task-specificity with partial transfer
Section 3 MemArena: 'We release the suite together with its adapters and wrappers'; accuracy is judge verdict under the Mem0 rubric with GPT-4o-mini as judge (Section 4, Models and search)
Section 4, Models and search: evolution uses T=8 rounds, P=4 parents, H=2 children, three seeds, seed std at most 0.8 points; search-based baselines share evolve split, meta agent and 64-child budget
llm_evaluation.rationale: A self-evolving hierarchical memory system for LLM agents with per-method program evolution, evidence-preserving routing, and a new evaluation suite (MemArena). Directly on-topic for agents, LLMs, and long-term memory. Quality is above average: four benchmarks, eleven baselines with shared search budgets, depth/channel/evolution ablations (Table 2), a McNemar-based acceptance test, and a record-disjoint split analysis (Table 4) that addresses evolve-split overfitting. Novelty is incremental: hierarchy is RAPTOR-like, routing to source turns is HippoRAG-like, and archive-based self-rewriting follows Darwin Godel Machine/MemPro; the contribution is the combination plus per-method attribution and statistical acceptance. Evidence is internally consistent (60.8 vs 55.2 avg = +10.1% relative; token ratios check out) but rests on a single LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini, Mem0 rubric) with no human-verification or judge-agreement analysis, and the PersonaMind benchmark is self-constructed. Generalizability is limited to conversational memory QA despite motivation citing web/SWE agents. Reproducibility is partial: MemArena release is claimed and algorithms/hyperparameters are specified, but LLM-driven code evolution is stochastic and no MemCodex code artifact is explicitly committed.

primary_link.title: MemCodex: Self-Programming Hierarchical Memory for Language Agents

papers.summary: Agent memory faces heterogeneous access needs: a single-hop question may require one piece of evidence, whereas a multi-hop question must combine evidence from multiple sources. Predefined memory workflows cannot adapt to these varying needs. Recent adaptive methods search or learn over memory components and their compositions, but the design space itself remains predefined. We introduce MemCodex, a self-evolving hierarchical memory system that organizes experience into executable memory program
papers.summary_zh: 語言代理在長期任務中累積大量經驗，但查詢需求高度異質：單跳問題只需一筆證據，多跳問題卻得整合多個來源。既有做法不是人工設計固定的記憶流程，就是在預先界定的模組空間中搜尋或學習策略，設計空間本身仍被寫死。作者提出 MemCodex，把經驗組織成可執行的記憶程式，分成 summary、graph、skill 三層衍生記憶置於唯讀的 raw 層之上，另以 kv memory 提供潛在記憶。每一層都有 admit、index、propose、score、route 五個固定介面的方法。系統以演化方式搜尋開放設計空間：每輪由 meta agent 從封存檔取出父代，只改寫某一層的某一個方法或開關某一層，使改動可歸因，再經記憶限制的合法性檢查與接受檢定（精確度不得下降、token 不得增加，僅提升精確度者須通過單尾 McNemar 檢定）。查詢時由粗到細走訪階層，route 決定停止、縮小或下降，最終答題一律回到原始對話輪，確保證據可追溯。作者同時釋出 MemArena 統一評測套件，涵蓋七個資料來源、十一種基線與兩種主幹模型。在 Qwen3.5-27B 上平均準確率 60.8%，較最強自適應基線 MemPro 高 5.6 分，讀取 token 少 3.4 倍、推論快 2.1 倍；GPT-5.4-mini 上亦領先 3.6 分。消融顯示證據保留帶來初始優勢，逐方法演化貢獻其餘多數增益。限制在於演化仍受限於固定層集與介面，且架構具任務特異性，跨任務僅部分可轉移。
papers.title: MemCodex: Self-Programming Hierarchical Memory for Language Agents
papers.title_zh: MemCodex：為語言代理自我編程的階層式記憶

links.title: ReTaCo: Residual-Target Control for On-Policy Distillation

evidence: Abstract & §1: loss decomposes as L_ren = D_KL(q^S||p^S) - log P (Eq. 1/8), proving the teacher is not a stationary point when m<1 (Prop 3.1, Cor 3.2).
§3.2–3.4: residual target t_β with r_β = m + β(1−m); Theorem 3.4 gives unique optimum with m ≤ P* ≤ r_β and dP*/dβ > 0; Prop 3.5 shows non-vanishing recovery gradients at β=0.
§4.1: 'the comparison with EOPD measures the complete training procedures rather than the residual target alone' — confounded baseline comparison.
Table 1 (§4.1): ReTaCo leads both baselines on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ across all three pairs; e.g., Qwen3.5-2B MATH500 71.73 → 79.85; OOD results 'less uniform' with mixed winners.
§4.2 Table 2: conditional-only forward supervision (R + mC) achieves highest scores on MATH500/OlympiadBench/AMC/AIME24; 'the mass constraint does not uniformly improve downstream accuracy'.

§5 Discussion and Limitations: equilibrium theorem holds only 'at a fixed prefix under the population objective; it does not guarantee convergence with evolving prefixes, stale policies, or clipped updates'.
Appendix D Table 4: numerical validation of predicted vs optimized selected mass with max ℓ1 error 4.13×10⁻⁸ in the conditional over S.

Appendix F Table 8 & F.1: full training/evaluation settings (AdamW lr 3e-6, BF16, k=16, α=1, β=0, avg@8 protocol, DAPO-Math-17k and Eurus-2-RL-Data), verl/OpenRLHF frameworks named; no code or artifact release stated.
Appendix F.2: 'No run averaging or uncertainty intervals are shown'; single diagnostic run; Appendix G Table 10 shows α and k sensitivity varies non-uniformly across tasks.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-methodology paper: identifies a precise flaw in renormalized top-k forward KL for on-policy distillation (hidden unit-mass target making the teacher non-stationary, Prop 3.1/Cor 3.2), proposes a β-controlled residual target with an O(k) communication budget and an unbiased single-sample reverse-KL estimator, with complete proofs, numerical equilibrium validation, three teacher–student pairs, component ablations, and honest mixed results (OOD non-uniform; β=0 default means the trimming knob is often not useful). Main weaknesses: the EOPD headline comparison is confounded by different frameworks, gates, and PPO-style updates (acknowledged in §4.1), no uncertainty intervals or multi-seed variance (Appendix F.2 states none are shown), no significance testing on modest point-estimate gains, and no code/data release despite very detailed settings. Novelty is incremental—a targeted fix to a recent preprint with related tail-aware distillation work already cited. Strongly in-scope for LLM/reasoning/code/training preferences; not a domain-application paper.

primary_link.title: ReTaCo: Residual-Target Control for On-Policy Distillation

papers.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generated prefixes with token-level teacher feedback, but transmitting or storing the teacher's full-vocabulary distribution at every token is costly. Entropy-aware OPD (EOPD) adds forward supervision to reverse KL to help the student recover plausible tokens it underestimates, using only the teacher's top-$k$ probabilities to limit cost. Because EOPD renormalizes these probabilities, its target assigns no mass to the omitted vocabulary. W
papers.summary_zh: 同策略蒸餾（on-policy distillation）讓學生模型在自己生成的脈絡上接受教師模型的 token 層級監督，但傳輸教師的完整詞彙分布成本高昂。熵感知同策略蒸餾（EOPD）在反向 KL 之外加入前向監督，並只取教師 top-k token 以降低通訊量；然而它把保留的機率重新正規化，等於把目標質量全押在選中集合上。作者證明此舉會產生隱性的「選中質量趨近 1」目標：即使學生的條件分布已與教師一致，−log P 仍持續推升選中質量，因此當被捨棄的詞彙具有正機率時，教師分布本身並非該損失的穩定點。為此提出 ReTaCo，把 top-k token 各自保留、其餘詞彙合併為單一殘差符號，並將殘差目標設為 (1−β)(1−m)，選中集合的相對機率維持不變；β=0 時保留教師質量分布，β 越大則把越多尾部質量移入選中集合。方法搭配單樣本估計器，其期望值等於全詞彙反向 KL，教師通訊量仍為 O(k)。理論上，作者在固定前綴下證明母體目標具唯一最佳解，其選中質量介於 m 與 m+β(1−m) 之間，且隨 β 單調遞增，並證實 β=0 時被低估的選中 token 仍能獲得非消失的回復梯度；數值最佳化亦驗證了預測的質量與條件分布。實驗涵蓋三組教師–學生配對，ReTaCo 在多數數學與程式碼基準上優於 EOPD。限制在於平衡點定理僅適用固定前綴下的母體目標，不保證動態前綴、策略滯後或梯度裁剪下的收斂；殘差裁剪的效果亦隨任務而異。
papers.title: ReTaCo: Residual-Target Control for On-Policy Distillation
papers.title_zh: ReTaCo：以殘差目標控制改良同策略蒸餾中的重新正規化偏誤

links.title: The Concrete-Arbitrary Gap: Kinship Reasoning in LLMs Is Not Indifferent to Presentation

evidence: §4/Table 1: 500 paired graphs show concrete-minus-arbitrary gaps of +35.6 (Qwen3.8-27B), +26.6 (Gemma 4 26B), +12.0 (Gemma 4 31B), +5.4 (Qwen3.8-Max) with exact McNemar p-values 7.71e-36 to 7.43e-6 and 10,000-resample graph-bootstrap CIs
§3.2: decoding protocol specified — temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, seed 20260914, vLLM 0.29.0 for local Qwen and llama.cpp b10917/Vulkan for Gemma, RTX 3090 hardware

§4: conservative scoring — invalid outputs counted as failures; local Qwen validity only 394/500 concrete and 253/500 arbitrary, with conditional accuracy (82.0% vs 57.3%) discussed as a post-treatment-selection pitfall

§4.2: pairing fixes gold answer, entity names, primitive meanings, and query direction, but authors concede it does not hold prompt length, syntax, or fact order fixed, so the effect is a 'presentation package'

§5.1: 512-token reasoning budgets close the gap (Qwen 83.6/84.8; Gemma 31B 99.6/99.8) with arbitrary-accuracy gains of 45.0/16.2/13.6 points relative to original off cells; short 32-token budgets sometimes hurt
§5.2/Table 3: inventory reduces Gemma 31B gap from +35.6 to +4.0 and coded output to +0.4; local Qwen reverses to -9.8 with inventory, showing instruction sensitivity and model heterogeneity
Limitations: benchmark is synthetic with a small family of short chains; mixed strict/final-line protocols across models; single decoding seed in most conditions; no mechanistic claim made
Data and Code Availability: frozen prompts, model responses, machine-readable results, evidence ledger, and analysis code at https://github.com/tompashby/concrete-arbitrary-gap
llm_evaluation.rationale: A carefully designed behavioral LLM-evaluation study squarely within preferred topics (LLMs, reasoning/CoT, prompting, benchmarking). The paired-graph design with explicitly defined nonce predicates cleanly rejects presentation-indifference across four models, with exact McNemar tests, graph-bootstrap CIs, Holm correction, and conservative scoring of invalid outputs; interventions (reasoning budgets, inventory/coded outputs) show the gap is instruction-sensitive and modifiable. Transparency is a major strength: mixed-protocol confounds, single-seed limits, the Qwen validity problem, and the prompt-length confound are all openly discussed rather than hidden. Novelty is moderate since content/presentation effects on LLM reasoning are established (Lampinen, Wu, Fatemi cited); the contribution is a refined paired test plus modifiability demonstrations. Generalizability is limited by a synthetic kinship task with a small relation family, four models, and one seed per cell; the paper itself scopes claims accordingly. Reproducibility is strong: frozen prompts, recorded responses, machine-readable results, and analysis code are released, with decoding parameters, quantization, and backends specified.

primary_link.title: The Concrete-Arbitrary Gap: Kinship Reasoning in LLMs Is Not Indifferent to Presentation

papers.summary: We test whether large language models solve formally matched kinship problems equally well when relations are expressed in familiar vocabulary or by explicitly defined nonce predicates. Across 500 paired graphs, concrete accuracy exceeds arbitrary accuracy by 35.6 percentage points in local Qwen3.8-27B, 26.6 in Gemma 4 26B-A4B, 12.0 in Gemma 4 31B, and 5.4 in Qwen3.8-Max. All four paired gaps are statistically resolved. Reasoning budgets and prompt-language interventions can substantially reduce
papers.summary_zh: 這篇論文檢驗一個直接的行為問題：當形式相同的親屬關係推理題，分別以熟悉的親屬詞彙與明確給出定義的自造述詞（nonce predicates）呈現時，大型語言模型是否表現一致？作者建構 500 組配對的合成親屬關係圖，同一圖的具體版本用日常親屬詞，任意版本改用 nuk、wug、tor 等明確界定意義的述詞，查詢對象與正確答案完全相同，並以配對圖為抽樣單位、採精確 McNemar 檢定與圖層級 bootstrap 信賴區間。主要結果是四個受測模型一致的「具體—任意落差」：地端 Qwen3.8-27B 為 35.6 個百分點，Gemma 4 26B 為 26.6，Gemma 4 31B 為 12.0，託管的 Qwen3.8-Max 為 5.4，且四個落差皆統計顯著。作者強調任意條件已提供英文定義，因此這不是「已知關係對未解讀符號」的比較，而是形式資訊以何種詞彙抵達模型的差異。後續介入顯示落差可修改：充足推理預算可大幅縮小落差（512 token 時三個地端模型幾近收斂），而顯示 15 個英文關係標籤的 inventory 或改用編碼輸出，甚至能讓 Qwen 的落差反號。限制方面，配對並未控制長度、語法與事實排序，評分協定在四個模型中不完全相同，Qwen-Max 的高正確率使可壓縮空間有限，且落差主要集中在 great-avuncular 類別。作者亦提醒，此結果只否定「完整呈現管線的呈現無差異性」，並不否定在成功解讀後存在不變的組合程序。其意義在於指出：明確給出定義並不足以讓自造述詞與熟悉詞彙一樣可用，而單張 RTX 3090 上的地端模型在此基準上可勝過託管旗艦模型，說明地端模型本身即具語言學研究價值。
papers.title: The Concrete-Arbitrary Gap: Kinship Reasoning in LLMs Is Not Indifferent to Presentation
papers.title_zh: 具體與任意之間的落差：大型語言模型的親屬關係推理並非對呈現方式無動於衷

links.title: Provably Tractable NFA-Constrained Language Generation via HMMs

evidence: Abstract: proposes NFA-LM, a polynomial-time engine for NFA-constrained generation with theoretical guarantees, inspired by FPRAS for #NFA
Section 1: motivates constrained generation via text detoxification, agentic function calling (Patil et al. 2024/2025), and structured SQL generation (Spider 2.0)
Section 5, Theorem 2: with probability ≥ 1-δ, TV distance between generated and target constrained distribution bounded by nε
Section 5, Theorem 3: time complexity O(|Σ|n²m³h²ε⁻²log(nmh)log(δ⁻¹))
Section 6, Table 2: NFA-LM succeeds on 500/500 instances (27.7-28.5s) vs Ctrl-G 43.4-45.2% (152.6-155.6s) and XGrammar 100% but lower quality (1.75-1.84 vs 2.44-2.48)
Section 6.2: exact brute-force completed for 232/500 instances; worst observed relative error ~0.00315 vs tolerance ε=0.1
Section 6, Models and Baselines: GPT-5.6 Luna, Qwen3.5-2B, Gemma-4-E2B; 128-state distilled HMMs; one NVIDIA L40S, 256s timeout
Limitations: guarantees bound error relative to exact HMM-guided decoding, not the HMM-to-LM approximation; context-free constraints and backreferences left open
Appendix E: LLM-judge rubric (fluency/coherence, 1-4 scale); judge is GPT-5.6 Luna, which is also a base model, and no human evaluation is reported
Appendix A: cached membership data structure for constant-time canonical-union membership checks
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM methodology paper: distribution-aware constrained generation from language models under Regex/NFA constraints, with applications to structured outputs, function calling, and text-to-SQL (Section 1), giving strong preference match. Novelty is solid but incremental: it generalizes Ctrl-G's DFA-tractable HMM approach to NFAs by adapting the #NFA FPRAS (Sections 1, 4), a meaningful extension since DFA conversion can be exponential (Table 1). Rigor is high on the theory side: complete proofs of Lemmas 1-3 and Theorems 1-3 with TV bound nε and polynomial time O(|Σ|n²m³h²ε⁻²log(nmh)log(δ⁻¹)) (Section 5, Appendices B-C), plus an honest Limitations section conceding the unbounded HMM-to-LM gap. Empirical rigor is moderate: single dataset (CommonGen, 500 instances, NFA states ≤ 50, length 1-64 tokens, Section 6), only two open models plus a proprietary one, no ablations on HMM size or (ε,δ) sensitivity, and generation quality judged by an LLM (GPT-5.6 Luna) that is also a base model, without human validation (Section 6.3, Appendix E). Evidence strength is supported by concrete numbers: 100% success in 27.7-28.5s vs Ctrl-G's 43-45% success at ~153s (Table 2), and worst relative error 0.00315 vs ε=0.1 on 232/500 brute-force-checkable instances (Section 6.2). Generalizability is decent in principle (any Regex constraint) but demonstrated narrowly; reproducibility benefits from detailed pseudocode (Algorithms 1-6), fixed parameters (ε,δ)=(0.1,0.1), hardware and prompt templates (Appendix E), but no code or artifact release is stated.

primary_link.title: Provably Tractable NFA-Constrained Language Generation via HMMs

papers.summary: Constrained generation aims to sample from language models (LMs) conditioned on hard constraints. Existing constrained-generation techniques for nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) constraints either distort the distribution or sacrifice efficiency. Theoretically, this task reduces to counting the length-$n$ sequences accepted by an NFA (#NFA), and the exact #NFA problem is #P-complete. Recent work has shown that #NFA admits a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme (FPRAS). Inspire
papers.summary_zh: 約束式生成要求語言模型輸出必須滿足硬性限制，例如規則表示式（Regex）所描述的格式。這類限制可用 NFA 表示，但給定前綴後計算「還有多少後續序列能滿足限制」本質上是 #NFA 計數問題，已知為 #P-complete，因此既有方法面臨兩難：XGrammar、PICARD 等遮罩式做法雖有效率，卻扭曲了真正的條件分布；Ctrl-G、GeLaTo 等保分布做法雖以 HMM 精確計算完成機率，卻只能處理 DFA，而一般 Regex 轉成 DFA 可能需要指數多個狀態。本文提出 NFA-LM，先從基礎語言模型蒸餾出 HMM，再把近期針對 #NFA 的 FPRAS（全多項式隨機近似方案）推廣到加權情形，估計 HMM 的完成機率，用以重新加權下一個 token 的分布。方法分為蒸餾、預計算與生成三階段，並透過正則化執行路徑（canonical run）、正則化聯集與中位數估計來控制重複取樣的相依性。理論上證明在溫和假設下，完成機率估計誤差落在 (1±ε) 之內，整體生成分布與目標分布的總變異距離不超過 nε，時間複雜度為多項式。實驗在 CommonGen 上以十類對 DFA 困難的 Regex 限制、500 個實例比較，NFA-LM 全部 500 個實例皆成功滿足限制，平均約 28 秒，而 Ctrl-G 成功率不到一半；在可暴力精算的 232 個實例中，最大相對誤差約 0.00315，遠低於 ε=0.1；文字品質也明顯優於 XGrammar。限制在於仍依賴蒸餾 HMM 作為語言模型完成機率的代理，且尚未涵蓋上下文無關語言與反向參照等非正規特性。
papers.title: Provably Tractable NFA-Constrained Language Generation via HMMs
papers.title_zh: 以 HMM 實現可證明可處理的 NFA 約束語言生成

links.title: ConflictGuide: AutoResearch Improves When Competing Behaviors Are Made Visible

evidence: Section 4 (Experimental Setup): both arms use Claude Code Opus 4.6; five model families (SpecB-FNO, SNGP, GCNII, ESN, TCM-Lite) with matched budgets, three search rounds, and formal retraining from frozen sources.

Section 4, Tables 2-6 and Appendix A Table 11: ConflictGuide lowers task error up to ~28% (ESN NRMSE 0.3173->0.2285, round 0) and conflict metric ~14% (ND-NMSE 0.0617->0.0530); some rounds show deltas within seed noise (e.g., SpecB-FNO round 2: 0.0398+/-0.0007 vs 0.0399+/-0.0007).
Section 4 (Ablation Studies), Table 7: guidance-only vs full ConflictGuide ablation shows complementary contributions of probe guidance and probe-based retention on SpecB-FNO and SNGP.
Appendix G (Tables 19, 21, 22): data isolation, frozen per-model retention thresholds, and 100+100 budgets (ESN 20+50) documenting controlled matched-arm design.
Appendix H, Table 8: multi-metric and trade-off-only prompt baselines compared on GCNII and SNGP round 2 only, with ConflictGuide best on all reported metrics.
Appendix I: transfer to Kimi K2.7 Code and AIDE (o4-mini/GPT-4.1-mini and GLM-5.3 configurations) on SpecB-FNO, noting probe-informed parent selection did not activate in one run.
Appendix E, Proposition 1: formal information-gain argument that probes strictly reduce squared/log loss for predicting conflict alleviation, with stated caveats about probe validity.
Appendix K: limitations — probe setup effort not uniformly costed, prespecified Stage-II timing, five model families only, and systematic evaluation of abstention left to future work.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Methodology paper on LLM coding-agent evolution loops (Claude Code Opus 4.6, Kimi K2.7 Code, AIDE) where the core contribution is probe-based competing-behavior feedback plus a two-stage search schedule — squarely matching Agents & Tool Use and Code & Programming preferences, with secondary relevance to Training & Optimization; LLMs are the vehicle rather than the studied artifact, and no Japanese/NLP, reasoning, or RAG content. Novelty is moderate-to-good: augmenting scalar-feedback auto-research with behavior probes and delayed feedback is a genuinely new angle per the related-work differentiation, though components (multi-metric feedback, retention rules, taxonomies) exist separately. Rigor is unusually high: matched-budget paired continuations from common branch points, source-only transfer with from-scratch retraining, data isolation (Appendix G, Table 19), frozen thresholds (Table 21), probe qualification, failure accounting, and probe-cost accounting (Table 25). Evidence supports the directional claim but with caveats: only 3 search rounds, some per-round deltas are within noise (e.g., SpecB-FNO rounds 1-2 differ by ~0.0003 NRMSE), baselines (multi-metric, trade-off prompt) tested on only two models in one round, and the delayed-feedback motivation rests on one model family. Generalizability is decent (five heterogeneous model families, three agent/framework settings) but each conflict was skill-instantiated with hand-designed probes and the authors admit applicability breadth and setup cost remain open (Appendix K). Reproducibility is strong via exhaustive appendix detail and supplementary code/skill, though the public repository is only promised upon acceptance. No out-of-scope cap applies since the language/agent methodology is central, not a pure domain application.

primary_link.title: ConflictGuide: AutoResearch Improves When Competing Behaviors Are Made Visible

papers.summary: When designing machine learning models, desirable properties are often in tension: improving one behavior can impair another, so task progress can depend on alleviating the conflict. LLM-based AutoResearch systems, which iteratively edit model code and retain edits based on scalar task-performance feedback, have largely ignored this trade-off. We find that scalar feedback supports broad exploration early in search, but it does not reveal how edits affect competing behaviors. In matched-budget ex
papers.summary_zh: 大型語言模型驅動的 AutoResearch 系統會反覆修改模型程式碼，並依純量任務指標決定是否保留修改；但純量回饋只顯示整體表現，無法揭露某次修改究竟如何影響彼此競爭的行為（例如頻譜主模態擬合與非主模態利用率、壓縮率與細節保留），因此搜尋常在後期停滯。作者先以對照預算實驗發現，若在任務增益趨緩後才導入競爭行為回饋，可將同時改善兩種行為的提案比例由 7.2% 提升至 13.1%，並把同時退化的比例由 29.0% 降至 20.7%，且能突破純量搜尋的平台期。據此提出 ConflictGuide：其可重用技能 ConflictGuide-Skill 以文獻歸納的 Root–Axis–Mechanism 分類法（9 個根因、6 個軸、110 個機制）辨識模型特有衝突，並設計可量測的探針指標，由程式代理以唯讀方式實作並於演化前完成合格性檢定。演化分兩階段：第一階段僅用任務回饋進行廣泛探索；第二階段加入探針回饋引導提案方向，並在任務增益僅屬邊際時，唯有探針顯示足夠衝突緩解才保留該修改。在五個異質模型家族（SpecB-FNO、SNGP、ESN、GCNII、TCM-Lite）與多種程式代理上，任務誤差最多降低 28%、衝突相關誤差最多降低 14%，消融顯示「引導」與「保留」機制互補。限制在於探針需模型專屬的建置與檢定成本，且僅適用於有充分證據支持的衝突情境。

papers.title_zh: ConflictGuide：讓相互競爭的行為可被觀察，可提升自動化研究成效

links.title: Growing an Agent/Prover Interface: Evolutionary Tool Design for Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving in Rocq and Lean

evidence: Section 4.1/Table 2: rocq-mcp-evolve accuracy .48/.80/.76/.88 (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus/Terra) vs control .17/.50/.43/.54 on held-out miniF2F-Rocq test, with sign test p<10^-21 vs control and p<3×10^-3 vs rocq-mcp
Section 2.3: anti-cheating system recompiles proofs in a clean directory and audits assumptions via Print Assumptions against standard axioms
Section 4.4: auto_close alone solves 52/244 (21%) of miniF2F-Rocq test, so automation does not fully explain gains
Section 4.3/Table 5: on putnam60 in Lean, lean-mcp-evolve accuracy (.33) matches control and trails lean-lsp-mcp (.42), but achieves best cost ($0.11) and wall time (64s)
Table 3: rocq-mcp-evolve averages 5.6 calls and 59.9k input tokens vs control's 5.9 calls and 79.0k, cutting output tokens roughly 4x
Section 2.1: mutation accepted if net gain ≥+2 in one difficulty bucket without dropping below −2 in any other; cost/wall time were secondary and validated no Phase 1 mutation

Reproducibility statement: server, harness, datasets, and table scripts released via anonymized OSF repository; process cannot be replayed deterministically; lean-mcp-evolve released only upon acceptance
Section 2.2/AI use statement: five project-scale Phase 2 tasks are AI-generated by the orchestrator and only author-reviewed
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core fit for Agents & Tool Use and LLM preferences: the paper evolves an MCP server (tool interface) for LLM agents doing theorem proving in Rocq/Lean, evaluated with frontier models. Methodological novelty is moderate—evolutionary/tool-evolution ideas exist (Darwin Gödel Machine, LATM-style works cited in Sec. 5), but applying validated per-feature evolution to prover interfaces with a frozen held-out benchmark is a fresh angle. Rigor is above average: disjoint test split, four models from two families, sign tests (Sec. 4.1, p<10^-21 vs control), a concrete anti-cheating verifier (Sec. 2.3), and an automation ablation (Sec. 4.4, 21% of solves attributable to auto_close). Evidence is solid but bounded by 2 runs/problem, small ad-hoc validation sets (dev60=60), a ±2-net-gain acceptance rule, and cost/time compared only on the intersection of solved problems (selection-prone, though disclosed in Table 2 caption). Generalizability is partially demonstrated: gains hold across models and on project-scale tasks, but Lean transfer shows no accuracy gain over control (Table 5), and contamination risk is admitted. Reproducibility is decent (code, harness, datasets, scripts on anonymized OSF/GitHub per Reproducibility statement) yet the evolution itself is non-deterministic via a proprietary orchestrator and lean-mcp-evolve is withheld until acceptance.

primary_link.title: Growing an Agent/Prover Interface: Evolutionary Tool Design for Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving in Rocq and Lean

papers.summary: Recent achievements in AI-assisted mathematics require intensive interaction of agents with proof assistants to generate machine-checked proof certificates. Agents interact with proof assistants such as Rocq or Lean through an interface that controls what the agent receives from the prover and the cost of these interactions. Today, these interfaces are adapted from tools designed for humans and not optimized for agents. We propose an evolutionary method where a frontier model incrementally propo
papers.summary_zh: 本文關注 AI 輔助數學中代理人與證明助理之間的互動介面問題。目前這類介面多沿用為人類設計的工具，未針對代理人最佳化，而介面直接決定每次互動的成本與效率。作者提出演化式方法：由前沿模型（Claude Fable 5）擔任協調者，逐步提出新功能，僅保留能改善較小模型整體表現的變更，並以正確率、每題解出成本與每題解出耗時三項指標驗證。實驗從僅暴露 Rocq 編譯器的最小伺服器出發，在 Rocq Workbook 的 dev60、hard70、mathcomp35 及 miniF2F-Rocq 驗證集上迭代，最終於第三天找到最佳設定，長出 rocq-mcp-evolve。在 miniF2F-Rocq 保留測試集上，搭配 Haiku 4.5、Sonnet 5、Opus 4.8 與 GPT-5.6 Terra 四款模型，其解題率、成本與耗時皆優於對照組與既有 rocq-mcp，Opus 上解題率提升約 30 個百分點、成本降低約 59%。專案級任務亦見改善。限制在於 Lean 移植版 lean-mcp-evolve 雖降低成本與時間，解題率仍低於 lean-lsp-mcp，且自動化戰術貢獻多集中於簡單題，實驗因前沿模型不可完全重現而僅能事後稽核。
